findings.reason: a worker cannot write a control that fires without first deciding which of the two structures holds the reuse, and an inert control is exactly the failure mode the done-when exists to prevent.
findings.text: the declared negative control "restores the per-read scope, and the scan-count case must then fail" presumes the reuse is implemented inside `resource_scan_scope` (the `_SCAN_SCOPE` ContextVar at reckon/resources.py:433), but the deliverable's key is "each resource file's own stat signature (path, mtime_ns, size)", a cache that holds per-file identifications outside the scope; arming the control by restoring the per-read scope would leave such a memo untouched and the scan-count assertion still green, so the control proves nothing

findings.reason: the mechanism as keyed reduces hashing but leaves the repeated walk the same evidence blames, so the node fixes half the measured cost and its "run the scan once" assertion cannot be written until the plan says what unit it counts.
findings.text: the deliverable's key "each resource file's own stat signature ... read in one walk without hashing" requires walking `docs_dir.rglob("*.html")` and stat-ing every file on each scan entry, so "The resource scan is computed once per tree state and reused across reads" is not achieved; §7's own kept head profile (logs/analysis-warm-head.txt) shows `_scan_resources` entered 4 times per warm roadmap read and 10 per warm audit read, and those repeats come from callers passing different `include_archived`/`include_legacy`/`ignore_invalid` arguments (distinct `_SCAN_SCOPE` keys, reckon/resources.py:477), which the per-file key does not name and cannot collapse
